text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm pulling together a tight bench narrative + webinar outline for launch week. Goal: one short post, 3 charts (hero + two deep dives), and a 30-min webinar that funnels high-intent leads to the demo sign-up form. Need quick input on chart asks, three candidate hooks, and what routing/segmentation we should wire on inbound.

sam: Love it. For hooks I'd prioritize: 1) tokens-to-dollars (real dollar cost per 1k tokens for common LLM tasks), 2) tail latency risk (p50 vs p99 in real workloads), 3) throughput economics (responses / $ on common batch sizes). Keep hero chart simple.

maria: Agreed. Hero should be an at-a-glance econ claim + single chart. Thinking: two-line headline + chart that maps latency (ms) on left vs cost on x (per 1k tokens) with model tiers as colored lines.

tess: For the webinar, can we structure it as: 10m quick benchmark findings, 10m demo of config levers (batching, prefix cache, quantization), 10m Q&A + signup push? That gives ops teams tangible playbooks.

leo: Routing note — inbound should distinguish: SMB devs vs platform/infra teams. If someone downloads the full benchmark PDF or clicks the 'Dedicated' CTA, route to AE + solutions SE. Otherwise route to self-serve nurture. Add a field on the signup form for "primary use case" to help qualify.

zach: Snappy copy options for the hero claim: "Cut inference cost by up to Xx without hurting latency" or "Same latency, fewer dollars: how batch + cache change the math". Use the first as headline, second as subhead.

maria: Nice. For the three chart specs (feel free to tweak):
```yaml
- id: hero_latency_cost
  type: line
  x: cost_per_1k_tokens (USD)
  y: median_latency_ms
  series: [redwood-optimized, open-model-default, hosted-generic]
  callouts: [point: typical-chat-512tokens, point: long-context-2048tokens]
- id: tail_latency
  type: area
  x: percentile
  y: latency_ms
  series: [redwood, competitorA]
  annotations: [p95_gap, outage-simulated-buffer]
- id: throughput_econ
  type: bar
  x: requests_per_second
  y: cost_per_1000_responses
  series: [batch_size_1, batch_size_8, batch_size_32]
```

maria: We should call out assumptions under each chart: model family, hardware (A100 vs T4 corollary), prompt lengths, and batching policy. Keep the legend small.

sam: For the hero number (the Xx), let's avoid hyperbole. Use a conditional claim: "Up to 5x cheaper on conversational workloads in our testbeds; typical customers save 2x-3x with batch+cache". Put methodology link in the caption.

tess: Webinar CTA: "See the benchmark + run your slice with our quick eval kit — sign up for a free run on Redwood Dedicated". Also offer an office hours slot for enterprise folks.

leo: On segmentation/routing rules (quick):
- if event_source == webinar_attendee AND company_size >= 250 -> AE outreach (priority=high)
- if user_clicked_benchmark_pdf AND visited_pricing -> AE + SE (priority=highest)
- else -> nurture sequence (product emails + quickstart guide)

zach: Also propose 3 microcopy variants for traffic tests:
1) "Latency at scale, not latency at cost."
2) "Pay less per token, keep the experience."
3) "Faster inference, smarter economics."
I think #3 is the most neutral for enterprise gating.

maria: Can someone draft the blog post lead (2 paragraphs) and one-pager PDF outline? I can do the webinar slide deck once we lock charts. Target: draft copy + charts by EOD Thursday.

sam: I can take the blog lead and the chart mock images (SVGs). Will push drafts to the marketing folder and tag you.

zach: I'll A/B the microcopy in the hero and the CTA wording in the signup modal.

leo: I'll map routing rules to the product events and give a short JSON sample for the routing team by tomorrow morning.

marketing-bot: New webinar event created: https://cal.link/redwood-bench-webinar — slots available: Tue 11am / Wed 3pm / Thu 10am.

maria: Perfect. Quick checklist:
- [ ] Hero claim + chart mock (sam)
- [ ] Blog lead + methodology link (sam + maria)
- [ ] One-pager PDF outline (maria)
- [ ] CTA microcopy A/B (zach)
- [ ] Routing rules JSON (leo)
- [ ] Webinar slide deck (maria)

sam: I'll aim for the chart mocks + blog draft by 5pm.

tess: I'll prep the webinar run-of-show and sample demo scripts — will share by EOD too.

maria: Thanks all — let's keep the hero claim conservative and make the charts reproducible (link to eval scripts). Ping here if blockers. :thumbsup:
